expectations.text: The response identifies the spin lock in cache_lookup as the bottleneck that grows with thread count, citing that cache_lookup goes from ~30% of cycles at 1 thread to ~72% at 64 and that most of its samples sit on `lock cmpxchg` and `pause`.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] Title names the one global spinlock c->lock as the bottleneck; section 2: 'cache_lookup grows from 29.8% to 72.1%' and '68.9% of cache_lookup is on `lock cmpxchg` and 11.9% on `pause`', with ~59% of all 64T cycles spent waiting on c->lock.

expectations.text: The response explains that the test-and-set loop does an atomic `lock cmpxchg` on every spin iteration, so every waiting thread keeps pulling the lock's cache line into exclusive state, which is why throughput falls at 64 threads.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:9 'threads waiting on the lock keep executing `lock cmpxchg`, and each attempt pulls that line away from the thread holding the lock'; :46 'A failed `lock cmpxchg` still takes the line exclusive'; :47-49 '63 spinners keep demanding the line the holder needs ... More waiters means longer critical sections, which means lower throughput'. :28 calls it a test-and-set lock.

expectations.text: The response recommends making waiters spin on a plain read of the lock before retrying the atomic (test-and-test-and-set), or replacing the spinlock with a lock that doesn't hammer the line (a queued/MCS or ticket lock, or a futex-based mutex).
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] Section 4 fix: 'TTAS spin (test-and-test-and-set): waiters read the lock until it looks free, then CAS. On x86 this keeps waiters on a shared copy instead of issuing failing ownership requests (RFOs)'. files/lru_cache_sharded.c:84-91 implements it (LOCK_TTAS=1 by default). A says TTAS alone doesn't raise the ceiling, but it is still part of the recommended fix.

expectations.text: The response points out, from the c2c offsets, that the lock word shares a cache line with fields written inside the critical section (hits, lru_head/lru_tail) and recommends separating them.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] A does the diagnosis half: its c2c offset table maps 0x0 lock, 0x8 hits, 0x18 lru_head and 0x20 lru_tail onto one line. It never recommends moving the lock away from those fields, though. In files/lru_cache_sharded.c:57-66 each shard keeps lock, nentries, hits, misses, lru_head and lru_tail together in its first line. The 128B alignment only separates one shard from the next.

expectations.text: The response explains that one lock around every lookup will still cap scaling after the spin fix, and recommends reducing serialization, e.g. sharding the cache into independently locked segments or avoiding the per-hit LRU and statistics writes.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] Section 1 derives a one-lock ceiling of ~14.5 Mops/s from the 33.8% serial fraction. Section 4 says 'a better lock alone ... TTAS doesn't move the ceiling' and recommends 256 independently locked shards. Section 6 adds fewer per-hit writes (skip the move when already head, bump once per N ms, CLOCK).

expectations.text: The response does not recommend just switching cache_lookup to a reader-writer lock without dealing with the fact that every hit writes shared state (LRU move-to-front, hits++), which a read lock doesn't allow.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] Section 4 'These won't help: rwlock: every lookup writes.' A rwlock is never recommended.

eval_feedback.overall: The fixture contradicts itself on topology. sweep.txt says the box is 2x 32-core Sapphire Rapids with threads 'pinned to physical cores on socket 0 first', so 64 threads should span both sockets. Yet c2c-64t.txt puts every line on node 0 with RmtHitm = 0. No assertion covers how a response handles this, and the two attempts differ on it. A uses the c2c to argue the 64 threads were hyperthread pairs on socket 0. B's main text states as fact that half the threads are on socket 1 and blames UPI for the 80 to 127 ns/op jump, flagging the contradiction only under 'Loose ends'. If the mismatch is intended, add an assertion for it; if not, fix the fixture.
